lineas.texto: Why don't the containers stacked on a ship fall off in a storm?
They're not glued, and they're not welded.
Every corner of every container has a steel block with a hole in it.
A twist lock drops into that hole, a handle turns, and two boxes lock together.
Lock every corner, and the whole stack moves like one tall block.
Down low, steel lashing rods run from the deck to the corners in an X.
And the heavy boxes go at the bottom, the light ones on top.
So when a wave rolls the ship thirty degrees, the stacks lean with it and hold.
When containers do go overboard, a box heavier than declared is often to blame.
